profiles.source_note: This page translates one campaign finance filing into plain English. The original filing should still be available alongside any public-facing summary.
profiles.summary_intro: This filing shows a campaign that still has a substantial cash reserve, but that spent more during the period than it raised.

filing_history.label: Q1 2026
filing_history.notes: The campaign reported strong early fundraising and ended the quarter with a larger reserve than it started with.

filing_history.label: Q2 2026
filing_history.notes: The campaign spent more than it raised in the second quarter, but still retained a substantial cash balance.

source_buckets.description: Political committees and PACs listed in the filing.

source_buckets.description: Small reimbursements, refunds, or rebates reported by the campaign.

spending_categories.title: Political donations
spending_categories.summary: The filing includes several $1,000 political donations to other committees or campaigns, including Friends of Thomas Paolino, Friends of Gordon Rogers, Friends of Elaine J. Morgan, and the Burrillville 250 Commission.

spending_categories.title: Digital advertising and communications
spending_categories.summary: Visible spending includes Facebook ads, Google ads, Mailchimp, Wix, and small WinRed-related charges.

spending_categories.title: Campaign materials and parade supplies
spending_categories.summary: Several Amazon purchases appear tied to parade candy, parade supplies, and general campaign materials.

spending_categories.title: Meals, meetings, and events
spending_categories.summary: The filing includes restaurants, coffee meetings, office appreciation meals, and event-related food purchases.

spending_categories.title: Travel and conference costs
spending_categories.summary: There are rideshare and parking expenses tied to conference travel and campaign-related events.

takeaways.title: Most visible support comes from individuals
takeaways.summary: Named individual donors account for the largest identified share of money coming in during this filing period.

takeaways.title: PAC money is present, but not dominant
takeaways.summary: The filing shows PAC support, but individual contributions still appear to be the main funding source in this period.

takeaways.title: The campaign spent more than it raised
takeaways.summary: This filing period ended with negative net movement, even though the campaign retained a large reserve overall.

takeaways.title: Spending was broad rather than concentrated
takeaways.summary: Expenditures span digital communications, political donations, materials, travel, and event costs instead of clustering in just one vendor category.

explainer_cards.title: Money raised
explainer_cards.summary: Money reported as coming into the campaign during the filing period, including individual donations, PAC contributions, online receipts, and occasional refunds.

explainer_cards.title: Money spent
explainer_cards.summary: Campaign spending during the filing period, such as ads, consultants, printing, food, events, travel, or donations to other political committees.

explainer_cards.title: Cash on hand
explainer_cards.summary: What the campaign reported still being available at the close of the filing period.

explainer_cards.title: Employer-linked donors
explainer_cards.summary: These are individual contributors grouped by the employer they listed on the filing. That is not always the same thing as a direct business donation.
